    Rust port of Project Meteor Server — a private-server emulator for FINAL FANTASY XIV v1.23b, the original 2010 1.0 release (not A Realm Reborn). Lobby, world, map, and web services in a single Cargo workspace, backed by SQLite and driving 1,142 upstream Lua content scripts.

Hi, I'm Sam 👋

Android & iOS Developer 📱 · Web Developer 🌐 · Hackathon Enjoyer 🏆

Bahamut is the new home of the FINAL FANTASY XIV 1.23b development I am working on moving forward.
If you'd like to participate as a developer or tester, or try our hosted server, join our Discord.

👨‍💻 About me

I'm a mobile developer who builds for Android (Kotlin) and iOS (Swift) by day, and dabbles in just about everything else by night — Rust, C/C++, TypeScript, and a healthy collection of emulators, game engines, and CLI tools. I love shipping things, learning new stacks, and the occasional weekend hackathon.

When I'm not writing apps, I'm usually reverse-engineering and reviving an old game I love. ⚔️

🐉 Final Fantasy XIV hobby projects

A big chunk of my free time goes toward preserving FINAL FANTASY XIV v1.23b — the original 2010 1.0 release, before A Realm Reborn. It's a piece of MMO history that the world otherwise lost, and bringing it back to life is my favorite playground.

  • ⚙️ Garlemald-Server — A Rust port of Project Meteor Server: a private-server emulator for FFXIV 1.0. Lobby, world, map, and web services in a single Cargo workspace, backed by SQLite and driving 1,142 upstream Lua content scripts.
  • 🚀 Garlemald-Client — A cross-platform Rust launcher for FFXIV v1.23b private servers (macOS / Linux / Windows).
  • 🔬 meteor-decomp & decomp-agents — Decompilation tooling for digging into the original client.
  • 🍎 XIV-1.0-Apple-Silicon-Installer — Getting the 1.0 client running on Apple Silicon.
  • 🐧 XIV-1.0-Linux-Installer — Getting the 1.0 client running on x86_64 Linux, across distributions.

🌐 It all lives at garlemaldsoftware.com — docs, idiot-proof quick-start guides, and downloads for every project in one place.

🛠️ Tech I work with

🤝 Find & follow great developers

This profile takes some inspiration from yumiaura and her followme project — a tool that discovers GitHub repositories, grades them with a local Ollama model, then follows promising authors and stars strong projects. It's a great reminder that the best part of GitHub is the people. If you're building something cool, say hi — I'm always happy to follow along. ⭐

📊 Stats

Thanks for stopping by — and if you make it back to Eorzea, I'll see you in 1.0. ✨
